realLifeExampleSummary: Vor einem Seminar landet Kaffee auf dem Oberteil; die Person erwartet danach, dass alle den Fleck stark beachten.
coverVisualThesis: A young adult is intensely focused on a visible coffee stain on their own shirt while the surrounding seminar room is mostly occupied with other people's conversations, phones and notes.

scenes.speechSection: Warum fühlt sich ein kleiner Fleck auf deinem Shirt plötzlich so an, als würde ihn jeder im Raum sehen?
scenes.viewerTakeaway: A small visible flaw can feel far more socially exposed to the person wearing it than the room's actual behavior suggests.
scenes.observableEvidence: At the entrance of a seminar room, a young adult looks down and partly covers a coffee stain on an off-white shirt while the people behind them are mostly talking, checking phones or writing instead of staring.
scenes.representationReason: The hook depends on the contrast between visible self-conscious behavior and the room's lack of concentrated attention, so human behavior is the clearest evidence.
scenes.dominantRelation: The stained-shirt person monitors the flaw while most surrounding people remain occupied with their own activity.
scenes.literalMetaphorWarning: Do not use a theatrical spotlight beam or stage lighting just because the concept is called Spotlight-Effekt.

scenes.speechSection: Dieses Gefühl passt zum sogenannten Spotlight-Effekt.
scenes.viewerTakeaway: The viewer learns the name of the effect without repeating the same character staging.
scenes.observableEvidence: The exact term is integrated as a large illustrated element beside a cropped coffee-stained shirt and seminar notebook from the same world.
scenes.representationReason: This beat names the concept; one large exact term is clearer than another social scene.
scenes.dominantRelation: Exact concept term paired with the same concrete stain cue.
scenes.literalMetaphorWarning: No literal spotlight, lamp cone or stage metaphor.

scenes.speechSection: Vereinfacht gesagt überschätzen wir manchmal, wie stark andere unser Aussehen, unsere Fehler oder unser Verhalten bemerken.
scenes.viewerTakeaway: The bias is a mismatch between how salient we feel to ourselves and how much others actually attend to us.
scenes.observableEvidence: One coherent comparison: left side shows the same person very close to a mirror, where the stain fills their attention; right side shows a wider seminar-room view where the person is only one element among several ongoing activities.
scenes.representationReason: A direct self-view versus room-view comparison explains overestimation more clearly than a definition card.
scenes.dominantRelation: Large self-focused flaw versus small social salience in the wider room.
scenes.literalMetaphorWarning: No spotlight beam or glowing aura.
scenes.camera: close mirror view contrasted with wide room view

scenes.speechSection: Du verschüttest vor einem Seminar Kaffee auf dein Oberteil und denkst danach bei jedem Blick sofort an diesen Fleck.
scenes.viewerTakeaway: A concrete everyday mishap can become the center of the person's attention.
scenes.observableEvidence: In a university hallway just before class, the recurring young adult holds a paper coffee cup and stares at the fresh stain on the off-white shirt, shoulders tense, while students move past naturally.
scenes.representationReason: The visible accident and immediate body reaction are the evidence, so a character moment is necessary.
scenes.dominantRelation: Fresh coffee spill versus immediate self-monitoring before entering the seminar.

scenes.speechSection: Für dich ist er ständig präsent, weil du genau weißt, dass er da ist.
scenes.viewerTakeaway: The flaw keeps re-entering the person's own attention.
scenes.observableEvidence: Close object-led view of the coffee stain on the off-white shirt, with one hand repeatedly tugging the open overshirt across it and a blurred notebook edge in the foreground.
scenes.representationReason: The stain itself is the point; a close object relation communicates persistent self-attention faster than another full-body scene.
scenes.dominantRelation: Visible stain repeatedly being covered by the wearer's hand.

scenes.speechSection: Die anderen im Raum beschäftigen sich gleichzeitig mit ihren eigenen Gesprächen, Handys, Notizen und Gedanken.
scenes.viewerTakeaway: Other people have competing attention demands and are not collectively monitoring one person's flaw.
scenes.observableEvidence: Wide lived-in seminar room: one pair quietly talks, one student checks a phone, another writes notes, another sorts papers; the stained-shirt person is present only as one normal figure among the room.
scenes.representationReason: The room's distributed attention is the evidence, so a wide environment-led composition is stronger than a close reaction shot.
scenes.dominantRelation: Multiple independent activities compete with attention to the stained-shirt person.
scenes.camera: wide seminar-room establishing shot with foreground depth

scenes.speechSection: In einer klassischen Studie ließen Forscher Teilnehmende mit auffälligen T-Shirts vor eine Gruppe treten.
scenes.viewerTakeaway: The original research used a concrete conspicuous-clothing setup.
scenes.observableEvidence: Early-2000s university psychology research room with a conspicuous graphic T-shirt on a chair, observer chairs arranged in a simple row, clipboard, old desktop monitor and plain institutional furniture; one participant approaches the setup while researchers remain secondary.
scenes.representationReason: The experimental setup and era are the key evidence, so the room and props should carry the frame rather than a generic researcher portrait.
scenes.dominantRelation: Conspicuous shirt and observer-room setup establish the study task.
scenes.literalMetaphorWarning: No readable brand or celebrity image on the T-shirt; use an abstract conspicuous graphic only.

scenes.speechSection: Die Teilnehmenden überschätzten, wie viele Beobachter sich später an das Motiv auf ihrem Shirt erinnern würden.
scenes.viewerTakeaway: Participants expected their shirt to stand out more than observers' behavior supported.
scenes.observableEvidence: One clean two-state comparison using four large observer figures only: left, the participant imagines all four observers looking directly at the shirt; right, in the actual room only one briefly glances while the others remain occupied with notes or conversation.
scenes.representationReason: The claim is a mismatch between expected notice and observed attention; a direct two-state comparison makes that discrepancy instantly readable without numeric clutter.
scenes.dominantRelation: Expected concentrated attention versus much more distributed observer attention.
scenes.literalMetaphorWarning: Do not invent percentages, charts or exact numeric values.

scenes.speechSection: Der Effekt zeigte sich nicht nur bei Kleidung: Auch eigene Beiträge in Gruppengesprächen wirkten den Sprechenden auffälliger als den anderen.
scenes.viewerTakeaway: People can also overestimate how much their own comments stand out in a group.
scenes.observableEvidence: Four stickman adults sit around a round discussion table. One speaker has just finished talking and watches the others tensely, while the other three naturally continue the discussion, check a note and respond to each other without dramatic focus on that speaker.
scenes.representationReason: The evidence is the mismatch between one speaker's self-conscious monitoring and the group's ordinary continuation, so human interaction is central.
scenes.dominantRelation: Self-conscious speaker versus normal distributed group attention.

scenes.speechSection: Eine Erklärung ist, dass wir von unserer eigenen intensiven Erfahrung ausgehen und die Perspektive anderer nur unvollständig korrigieren.
scenes.viewerTakeaway: Our own vivid perspective can serve as the starting point when estimating what others notice.
scenes.observableEvidence: One simple two-step illustrated mechanism: a large close mirror view of the recurring person noticing the stain flows through one single arrow into a much wider room view where the stain occupies only a tiny part of the scene.
scenes.representationReason: The beat describes a perspective-adjustment mechanism; one simple two-step schema is clearer than another social scene and stays mobile-readable.
scenes.dominantRelation: Vivid self-view narrows into a wider others' perspective but does not fully disappear.
scenes.literalMetaphorWarning: No abstract brain icons, energy fields or dense arrows.

scenes.speechSection: Das bedeutet aber nicht, dass niemand deinen Fehler bemerkt oder dass jeder peinliche Moment unsichtbar bleibt.
scenes.viewerTakeaway: The effect is an overestimation bias, not invisibility.
scenes.observableEvidence: Tight object-led frame on the same coffee stain; at the edge of frame a cropped stickman face briefly turns its eyes toward the stain before moving on, while most of the background remains out of focus.
scenes.representationReason: The nuance is best shown by one real glance toward the flaw without turning the moment into a full social confrontation.
scenes.dominantRelation: The flaw is genuinely noticed once, but only briefly.
scenes.camera: tight stain close-up with cropped glance cue

scenes.speechSection: Jemand kann den Fleck, einen Versprecher oder eine falsche Antwort durchaus sehen – nur oft weniger stark, als du erwartest.
scenes.viewerTakeaway: A social mistake can be noticed without becoming the whole room's focus.
scenes.observableEvidence: In the seminar, the recurring young adult gives a visibly uncertain wrong answer with one hand half-raised. One nearby student looks up, while the others keep writing or looking at the lecturer.
scenes.representationReason: The sentence is about partial social notice of a mistake; the distribution of visible reactions across people is the core evidence.
scenes.dominantRelation: One person notices the mistake while the rest of the room stays on task.
scenes.literalMetaphorWarning: Do not show all three examples at once; use only the wrong-answer situation.

scenes.speechSection: Spätere Forschung zeigte außerdem: Menschen überschätzen auch, wie deutlich Schwankungen ihrer Leistung anderen auffallen.
scenes.viewerTakeaway: People can overestimate how much observers notice changes in their performance across moments.
scenes.observableEvidence: One coherent two-state videogame comparison with the same player and one observer: left, the player performs very well and looks toward the observer; right, the player has a poor round and again checks the observer, who remains similarly occupied in both states.
scenes.representationReason: The research claim concerns perceived performance variability, so the same person across two performance states is the clearest representation.
scenes.dominantRelation: Large perceived swing in one's own performance versus relatively stable observer attention.
scenes.literalMetaphorWarning: No readable score numbers or invented quantitative results.

scenes.speechSection: Eine nützliche Gegenfrage lautet: Würde mir derselbe kleine Fehler bei einer anderen Person wirklich lange im Gedächtnis bleiben?
scenes.viewerTakeaway: A perspective-taking question can interrupt self-focused assumptions.
scenes.observableEvidence: A real illustrated desk scene with a phone, closed notebook and coffee cup; one large note card is the focal object and carries the exact German question in large type.
scenes.representationReason: The wording itself is the useful mental prompt, so the exact question should lead the frame in a real-world desk context rather than a presentation slide.
scenes.dominantRelation: One practical question becomes the single focal object.
scenes.literalMetaphorWarning: No extra labels or paragraph text.

scenes.speechSection: Dieser Perspektivwechsel kann helfen, den eigenen Moment wieder als einen kleinen Teil der gesamten Situation zu sehen.
scenes.viewerTakeaway: Widening perspective reduces the visual dominance of the self-focused moment.
scenes.observableEvidence: Very wide seminar-room view from the back corner. The recurring young adult is only one person among several students, tables, bags and ongoing activities; no one is centered and the room feels balanced and ordinary.
scenes.representationReason: The point is scale and context, so a wide environment composition makes the individual moment visibly smaller without needing a diagram.
scenes.dominantRelation: One person's awkward moment becomes one small element inside a much larger social environment.
scenes.literalMetaphorWarning: No literal zoom-out graphic or spotlight cone.

scenes.speechSection: Du erlebst deinen Fehler von innen und in voller Lautstärke. Andere sehen oft nur einen kurzen Ausschnitt davon.
scenes.viewerTakeaway: Our own experience is continuous and intense, while other people usually encounter only a brief fragment of it.
scenes.observableEvidence: After the seminar, a wide university hallway shows the recurring young adult walking calmly with the crowd. Different people peel off toward stairs, doors and conversations; the coffee stain is still faintly visible but no longer dominates the composition.
scenes.representationReason: A moving crowd and reduced visual importance of the stain provide a stronger closing image than another close-up or text card.
scenes.dominantRelation: The once-dominant flaw becomes a small detail inside everyone else's separate movement and attention.
scenes.literalMetaphorWarning: No sound-wave graphics or literal loudness symbols.
